name: Celeriac
grown_as: Celeriac, a biennial grown as an annual for its swollen stem base, sown under cover in early spring and lifted in autumn and winter. Varieties differ little in look.
habit: Year 1: a spreading rosette of glossy leaves 40 to 60 cm high from the top of a knobbly round swelling 8 to 15 cm across that sits half above the soil, with a dense tangle of roots beneath. Year 2: a branched, grooved flowering stem 60 to 100 cm.

leaf.arrangement: A rosette from the top of the swelling
leaf.type: Compound: once pinnate, with 2 to 4 pairs of leaflets and one at the end (as celery)
leaf.leaflets: Leaflets on short stalks or none, set well apart; each broad, roughly diamond- to wedge-shaped and deeply cut into three lobes
leaf.outline: Whole leaf 20 to 40 cm; leaflets 3 to 6 cm, broadly wedge- to diamond-shaped
leaf.base: Leaflets wedge-shaped at the base; leaf stalk widening into a sheath
leaf.margin: Lobed, the lobes coarsely toothed on their outer half; the wedge-shaped base untoothed
leaf.surface: Smooth, hairless and glossy; strong smell of celery when crushed
leaf.stalk: Long, ribbed, solid to slightly hollow, thinner than celery's, green

flower.form: Small, loose compound umbels of tiny flowers
flower.petals: Five free, tiny petals, tips rolled in
flower.centre: Five stamens and a small swollen disc
flower.carried: Small umbels with 4 to 12 short unequal spokes, on very short stalks or none, set opposite the leaves along the stems as well as at the tips
flower.size: Flowers about 1 mm; umbels 2 to 5 cm across
flower.season: June to August of the second year

fruit: Tiny round to oval paired seeds about 1.5 mm, ridged, brown, aromatic.
seedling: Two small oval seed leaves on short stalks, then first true leaves rounded and three-lobed with toothed edges. Very slow and small at first.
winter: Hardy to moderate frost; often left in the ground under straw or a mulch, the outer leaves dying back to a tuft of small inner leaves.

leaf: once pinnate: pairs of broad lobed leaflets along one stalk and one at the end
leaflets wedge-shaped at the base, three-lobed and toothed on their outer half
bloom: small loose umbels of tiny greenish-white flowers
seed: a tiny round ridged brown seed, about 1.5 mm
seedling: first true leaves rounded, three-lobed and toothed
young: a rosette of glossy pinnate leaves
the stem base starting to swell at the soil
crop: a round knobbly cream-brown swelling sitting half above the soil
a dense tangle of roots underneath it
leaf stalks rising from its top, scars of old leaves on its shoulders
flower: many small greenish-white umbels set along the stems
seedhead: small umbels of tiny brown seeds on short spokes

look_alikes: Celery is the same species grown for its thick leaf stalks, without the swelling. Wild celery grows by the sea. Parsnip leaves are hairy and dull, its flowers yellow. Fool's water-cress has once pinnate leaves too, but lives in water.
